# pinray

> Cross-platform screen and system-audio capture for Rust. pinray uses each OS's native capture API (XDG portal + PipeWire and X11 on Linux, ScreenCaptureKit on macOS, DXGI / Windows Graphics Capture + WASAPI on Windows) and returns raw video and audio frames with stride, pixel format, timestamps, sequence numbers, and drop signals. It doesn't encode: pipe frames into ffmpeg, WebRTC, wgpu, or your own pipeline.

This page is the whole public API of `pinray` 0.2 plus the rules an agent needs to write correct code against it. It was checked against the source (`crates/core/src/*.rs`, `crates/pinray/src/lib.rs`). If anything here disagrees with docs.rs/pinray-core, docs.rs wins.

## Install

```toml
[dependencies]
pinray = "0.2"
```

- Linux build needs PipeWire headers and clang: `libpipewire-0.3-dev clang` (Debian/Ubuntu), `pipewire clang` (Arch), `pipewire-devel clang` (Fedora). Runtime needs a PipeWire daemon, plus XDG Desktop Portal for Wayland video.
- macOS 13.0+ and Windows 10+ (WGC needs 1903+) need nothing extra.
- MSRV is Rust 1.88. pinray is pre-1.0: minor versions may break the API, so depend on `"0.2"`.

## Quick start

```rust,no_run
use std::time::Duration;
use pinray::{
    AudioCapture, CaptureEvent, CaptureSession, PinrayError, SourceId, VideoCaptureTarget,
};

fn main() -> Result<(), PinrayError> {
    let mut session = CaptureSession::builder()
        .video_target(VideoCaptureTarget::Display(SourceId::new("auto")))
        .audio(AudioCapture::SystemMix)
        .build()?; // Wayland: blocks on the portal dialog. macOS: permission check.
    session.start()?;

    for _ in 0..300 {
        match session.next_event(Some(Duration::from_millis(500))) {
            Ok(CaptureEvent::Video(f)) => {
                let pixels = f.to_tight_bytes(); // BGRA, row padding removed
                println!("{}x{} seq={} bytes={:?}", f.width, f.height, f.sequence,
                         pixels.map(|p| p.len()));
            }
            Ok(CaptureEvent::Audio(a)) => println!("{} Hz x{}", a.sample_rate, a.channels),
            Ok(CaptureEvent::Gap(g)) => eprintln!("dropped: {:?}", g.reason),
            Ok(CaptureEvent::End) => break,
            // Not an error: DXGI sends nothing while the screen is idle,
            // X11 polls, Wayland only sends on screen changes.
            Err(PinrayError::Timeout(_)) => continue,
            Err(e) => return Err(e),
        }
    }
    session.stop()
}
```

Never write `session.next_event(..)?` in a capture loop: an idle desktop returns `Err(PinrayError::Timeout)` and `?` ends the program. Match `Timeout` and continue, as above.

Audio only: skip `.video_target` and read with `session.next_audio(timeout)` on Linux/Windows. On macOS, read audio from `next_event` as `CaptureEvent::Audio`; `next_audio` returns `BackendNotSelected` there (#34). Audio-only shows no dialog on Linux/Windows; macOS still needs Screen Recording permission.

## API

`pinray::CaptureSession::builder() -> pinray::SessionBuilder` (or `SessionBuilder::default()`). Every setter takes and returns the builder by value. Nothing is validated until `build()`:

- `.video_target(VideoCaptureTarget)`: a display or window. Omit for audio-only
- `.audio(AudioCapture)`: only `AudioCapture::SystemMix` works; `Microphone(_)` makes `build()` fail with `Unsupported`
- `.backend_preference(BackendPreference)`: default `Auto`
- `.pixel_format(PixelFormat)`: default `Bgra8888` (native everywhere); `Rgba8888` costs a CPU swizzle (about 3x the CPU in one 1080p60 Wayland measurement); other formats are unreliable (Windows rejects them, Wayland falls back to BGRA, #31). Always read `frame.pixel_format`
- `.cursor_mode(CursorMode)`: default `Embedded`; DXGI never draws the cursor
- `.crop_rect(Option<Rect>)`: default `None`; ignored on Wayland (#30); macOS output is upscaled (#22)
- `.frame_rate(Option<u32>)`: default `Some(60)`. A maximum, not a guarantee. `None` = uncapped on Wayland/DXGI/WGC, 30 fps on X11, 60 fps on macOS. `Some(0)` fails validation
- `.queue_depth(u32)`: default `2`; frames buffered before new ones are dropped. `0` fails validation
- `.restore_token(impl Into<String>)`: Wayland portal token from a previous session; skips the dialog if the compositor still honors it
- `.color_space(Option<ColorSpace>)`: stored but no backend acts on it (#32); read `frame.color_space` instead
- `.config() -> &CoreSessionConfig`: the config built so far
- `.build() -> Result<CaptureSession, PinrayError>`: validates, opens the platform backend, returns a stopped session

`CaptureSession` methods:

- `.start() -> Result<(), PinrayError>` / `.stop() -> Result<(), PinrayError>`: idempotent; a session can be restarted. Call `stop()` when done
- `.next_event(Option<Duration>) -> Result<CaptureEvent, PinrayError>`: next video frame, audio packet, or gap. `None` blocks forever; `Some(Duration::ZERO)` polls without blocking. On Linux and Windows, where video and audio are separate backends, pending audio comes first and one call can wait up to 2x the timeout. On macOS both arrive from one ScreenCaptureKit stream with a single timeout
- `.next_audio(Option<Duration>) -> Result<AudioFrame, PinrayError>`: audio only (not on macOS, see above)
- `.backend_info() -> &BackendInfo`: which backend was picked; log it, it differs per machine
- `.restore_token() -> Option<String>`: Wayland token to persist for next run; `None` elsewhere
- `.is_running() -> bool`, `.config() -> &CoreSessionConfig`

Free functions:

- `pinray::enumerate_sources() -> Result<Vec<CaptureSource>, PinrayError>`: displays, windows, and audio sources. Enumerate right before building a session (window ids die with the window). On macOS this triggers the permission check
- `pinray::available_backends() -> Vec<BackendInfo>`: backends compiled in for this OS

`pinray::Result` is not exported. Write `Result<T, pinray::PinrayError>` (or your own alias).

## Types

```rust
enum CaptureEvent { Video(VideoFrame), Audio(AudioFrame), Gap(GapEvent), End }
// `End` is not emitted by any backend today: stop your loop yourself.

struct VideoFrame {
    stream_time_ns: i64,   // monotonic within a session, same clock as AudioFrame;
                           // epoch: boot on macOS/Windows, process start on Linux
    sequence: u64,         // +1 per captured frame; a jump = frames dropped
    width: u32,
    height: u32,
    stride: u32,           // bytes per row in FrameData::Host; can exceed width * bpp
    pixel_format: PixelFormat,
    color_space: Option<ColorSpace>,
    data: FrameData,
    damage: Option<Vec<Rect>>, // changed regions, when the backend knows
}
impl VideoFrame {
    fn to_tight_bytes(&self) -> Option<Vec<u8>>; // padding stripped; None for non-Host / YUV
}

enum FrameData {
    Host(Vec<u8>),                      // the only variant produced today
    Dmabuf(DmabufFrame),                // reserved
    CvPixelBuffer(CvPixelBufferHandle), // reserved
    D3D11Texture(D3D11TextureHandle),   // reserved
}

enum PixelFormat { Bgra8888, Rgba8888, Rgb888, Nv12, I420 }
impl PixelFormat { fn bytes_per_pixel(self) -> Option<usize>; } // 4, 4, 3, None, None
enum ColorSpace { Srgb, DisplayP3, Bt709, Bt2020 }
enum CursorMode { Embedded, Hidden }
struct Rect { x: i32, y: i32, width: u32, height: u32 } // relative to the source's top-left

struct AudioFrame {
    stream_time_ns: i64,   // same clock as VideoFrame::stream_time_ns
    sequence: u64,         // a jump = packets dropped
    sample_rate: u32,      // e.g. 48_000
    channels: u16,
    sample_format: SampleFormat,
    data: AudioData,
}
enum SampleFormat { I16, I32, F32, F64 }  // little-endian; F32 is the common case. NOT S16/S24/U8
enum AudioData { Interleaved(Vec<u8>), Planar(Vec<Vec<u8>>) }

enum VideoCaptureTarget { Display(SourceId), Window(SourceId) }
enum AudioCapture { SystemMix, Microphone(SourceId) }

struct SourceId(pub String);  // SourceId::new("auto") = primary display, no enumeration needed
// Ids are opaque: "display:<name>" (Linux), "display:\\.\DISPLAY1" (Windows),
// "window:<id>", "audio:system-mix". Take them from enumerate_sources().
enum CaptureSource {          // an enum, NOT a struct with .id/.name/.kind
    Display(DisplaySource),
    Window(WindowSource),
    SystemAudio(AudioDeviceSource),
    Microphone(AudioDeviceSource), // never returned today
}
struct DisplaySource { id: SourceId, name: String, width: u32, height: u32, scale_factor_milli: u32, is_primary: bool }
struct WindowSource { id: SourceId, title: String, app_name: Option<String> }
struct AudioDeviceSource { id: SourceId, name: String, is_default: bool }

enum GapReason { Dropped, FormatChanged, BackendRestarted, Unknown }
struct GapEvent { stream_time_ns: i64, reason: GapReason, dropped_frames: Option<u32> }

enum BackendPreference { Auto, LinuxWaylandPortal, LinuxX11, MacScreenCaptureKit, WindowsDxgi, WindowsWgc }
enum BackendKind { LinuxWaylandPortal, LinuxX11, LinuxPipeWireAudio, MacScreenCaptureKit, WindowsDxgi, WindowsWgc, WindowsWasapi }
struct BackendInfo { kind: BackendKind, supports_audio: bool, zero_copy: bool, notes: &'static str }
// field is `notes` (not `note`), a &'static str (not Option<String>)

enum PinrayError {
    InvalidConfig(String), BackendUnavailable(String), BackendNotSelected,
    Timeout(Duration), Unsupported(String), Platform(String),
}
```

All of these are re-exported at the crate root (`pinray::VideoFrame`, etc.). `SessionConfig` is exported as `pinray::CoreSessionConfig`.

## Errors

- `Timeout(_)`: nothing arrived in time. Normal; call again
- `InvalidConfig(_)`: fix the builder call (nothing to capture, zero `frame_rate`/`queue_depth`, empty or out-of-bounds crop)
- `BackendUnavailable(_)`: this backend can't run here (no Wayland session and no `DISPLAY`, macOS < 13, forcing another OS's backend)
- `Unsupported(_)`: unimplemented option (microphone, some pixel formats). Also returned when the user cancels the Wayland portal dialog (#29)
- `Platform(_)`: OS API failure, macOS Screen Recording permission denied, or the captured window closed
- `BackendNotSelected`: `next_audio` on a session without a separate audio backend (no audio, or macOS)

## Rules agents get wrong

1. **Stride.** `stride` can exceed `width * bytes_per_pixel`. Copying `FrameData::Host` straight into an encoder or `rawvideo` pipe skews every row after the first. Use `frame.to_tight_bytes()`.
2. **BGRA, not RGBA.** Default frames are BGRA. Request `Rgba8888` or swap channels yourself.
3. **Frame rate is a maximum.** Wayland, DXGI, and WGC send frames on screen changes, not on a clock. For video files, pace output with `stream_time_ns` (duplicate the last frame to fill gaps) instead of declaring a constant rate. Worked example: the "Frame rate" section of the getting-started guide (link below).
4. **Timeouts are flow, not failure.** See the quick start.
5. **Threading.** `CaptureSession` is `Send` but not `Sync`: move it into one capture thread and send frames out over a channel. Both read methods take `&mut self`, so one thread owns all reads.
6. **Wayland picks the source, not you.** The portal dialog decides what's captured; a `Display` id from `enumerate_sources()` is informational only. Wayland lists displays (no windows) without a dialog.
7. **macOS display sizes.** `DisplaySource` `width`/`height` are points, `scale_factor_milli` is a placeholder 1000, `is_primary` is always false (#23).
8. **Logging.** pinray logs through `tracing`. `RUST_LOG=debug` only works if your app installs a subscriber, e.g. with `tracing-subscriber` (feature `env-filter`): `tracing_subscriber::fmt().with_env_filter(tracing_subscriber::EnvFilter::from_default_env()).init();`.
9. **Mocks and custom backends.** Depend on `pinray-core`, implement `VideoBackend` / `AudioBackend` and a `BackendResolver`, then configure a `pinray_core::SessionBuilder::new()` with the usual setters and finish with `.build_with_resolver(&resolver)` instead of `.build()`. The crate-level docs on docs.rs/pinray-core have a complete mock backend. Useful for testing frame handling without a desktop. Backends must return `Timeout` on timeout and treat `Some(Duration::ZERO)` as a non-blocking poll.

## Other known issues

- If audio fails to start, `start()` leaves video running and `stop()` won't release it; drop the session (#33)
- Audio queues are bounded: Linux and Windows drop the oldest packets, macOS drops new ones
